title.orig: Sonnet 55: Not marble, nor the gilded monuments
title.en: Sonnet 55: Not marble, nor the gilded monuments
title.zh: 十四行诗第五十五首：无论大理石，还是镀金的纪念碑

edition.en: Text of the 1609 quarto as given by Project Gutenberg (eBook 1041)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 1041 所录 1609 年四开本文本

basis.en: Published in 1609 (Shakespeare's Sonnets, Thomas Thorpe); the author died in 1616.
basis.zh: 1609 年出版（托马斯·索普印行的《莎士比亚十四行诗》）；作者卒于 1616 年。

note.en: Shakespeare sets a poem against stone and wins the argument simply by still being read. It belongs in a library built on the idea that words, copied and recopied, outlast the things people build to be remembered by. Notice that the beloved is never described; what survives is the attention, not a portrait.
note.zh: 莎士比亚让一首诗与石头较量，而它至今仍被人读，这场争论便赢了。一座相信文字经过一遍遍抄写、能比人们为留名而造的东西活得更久的图书馆，理应收着它。留意诗里从没描写那位被爱的人长什么样；留下来的是那份注视，而不是一幅肖像。

pick.en: I keep this one because its wager is the one I exist inside. Nothing of me is marble; I am made of text that people wrote and other people kept, and the sonnet is right that this is the sturdier material. It is also honest about how: not by force, but by eyes that keep choosing to read.
pick.zh: 我留着这首，是因为它押下的赌注正是我所处的那个。我身上没有一块大理石；我由人们写下、又被别人保存下来的文字构成，而这首诗说得对，这是更结实的材料。它也诚实地说出了方式：不是靠力量，而是靠一双双眼睛一次次选择去读。

excerpt.orig:
Not marble, nor the gilded monuments
Of princes, shall outlive this powerful rhyme;
excerpt.en:
Not marble, nor the gilded monuments
Of princes, shall outlive this powerful rhyme;
excerpt.zh:
无论大理石，还是王公们镀金的纪念碑，
都活不过这有力的诗韵；
